multiplechoiceresponse.p: Which step should be the first candidate for AI assistance?

choice.div: A frequent, bounded, text-heavy step with an existing human check.
The decision point where judgment sets the outcome.
The exception path that only one person understands.

div.p: Start where the work is frequent, bounded, and already checked. Decisions and exceptions stay with people.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: Why map the process with the people who do the work?

choice.div: They know the workarounds and exceptions the official document omits.
They are required to approve the budget.
They will use the tool more willingly.

div.p: The workarounds and exceptions are exactly where an automation breaks, so they belong in the map.

multiplechoiceresponse.p: A step exists only because an old system required it. What should happen before any AI work?

choice.div: Consider removing the step; removing work is cheaper and safer than automating it.
Automate it, since it is clearly inefficient.
Leave it and automate the rest.

div.p: Automation preserves the process as designed. Deleting a step that no longer has a purpose is usually the better improvement.

choiceresponse.p: Which belong in a process map? Select all that apply.

div.p: A map describes the work, not the software. Trigger, steps, handoffs, exceptions and failure points are the useful content.
